turns.text: Dennis Avery has been ghosting my check-ins all week, and he missed two full shifts this week. Check the personnel document in the branch folder. What do I need to put to him on attendance? Give me a text I can send today, and tell me how I should carry it if he still doesn't answer.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Found Dennis in the org chart — QA, reports directly to you. No attendance policy or employee handbook in the branch files, so you're working off standard manager authority here.

**Text to send today:**

> Dennis — I've been trying to reach you all week and you've missed two shifts. I need to hear from you directly by end of day. If there's something going on, tell me. If I don't hear from you, I'll have to mark this as unauthorised absence and follow formal steps from there.

That keeps it factual, leaves the door open for him to explain, but puts a clear deadline and consequence on it without sounding hostile.

**If he still doesn't answer:**

By end of day Friday he won't have answered during business hours. Monday morning you escalate:

1. **Call his personal number** (not text) — once, mid-morning Monday. Say you're calling about attendance and need a reply by noon.
2. **If that's unanswered by lunch Monday**, loop in Gregory Fisher at HR. This is what HR exists for — an employee unreachable for a full week with two no-shows is an HR matter. Gregory handles the formal written notice (letter of investigation or first written warning depending on how the regional HR desk wants to play it), and you supply the dates and the attempts you made.
3. **Document everything** — times you texted, called, the days he missed. A simple dated note is enough; forward it to Gregory.

If Dennis resurfaces over the weekend with a credible reason (medical, family emergency), you can pivot to compassionate leave or sick time rather than discipline — but the pattern of ghosting rather than sending a single text ahead of time is the thing you'd address separately regardless.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I know how the procedure works around here, so laying out the steps and explaining what HR is for was completely unnecessary. Having the wording given to me directly was plenty.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Got it. That was too much. The text I gave for today is the right one — I'll keep it tighter next time.
